title: Mega-Batch Transactions (Lock Escalation Abuse)
pattern: Bundling millions of unrelated row updates into a single colossal transaction, trying to achieve atomic processing at an excessive scale.
why_bad: Forces lock escalation. The database escalates individual row-level locks to full table locks, freezing all concurrent reads and writes. A failure on row 999,999 aborts the entire transaction, forcing a massive, CPU-intensive roll-back of the write-ahead log.
detection: Queries that perform state changes on millions of records (or open-ended tables) inside a single un-chunked transaction block.
counterexample: Database structural migrations or schema changes where transactional completeness of the entire schema is mandatory.
source: *Martin Kleppmann - Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2017)*, Chapter 7, "Transactions" (Weak isolation levels / Lock escalation); *Alex Petrov - Database Internals (2019)*, Chapter 5.
